The '''International Linear Algebra Society (ILAS)''' is a professional mathematical society organized to promote research and education in [[linear algebra]], [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix theory]] and [[Numerical linear algebra|matrix computation]]. It serves the international community through conferences, publications, prizes and lectures.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/who-we-are/|title=ILAS: Who we are|website=International Linear Algebra Society|date=25 November 2020 |access-date=April 2, 2021}}</ref> Membership in ILAS is open to all mathematicians and scientists interested in furthering its aims and participating in its activities.

==History==

ILAS was founded in 1989.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://archives.math.utk.edu/societies.html|title=Math Archives|access-date=March 11, 2020|archive-date=March 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200328173530/http://archives.math.utk.edu/societies.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Hershkowitz|first=D.|date=1989|title=News Items|journal=IMAGE: Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society|volume=4}}</ref>  Its genesis occurred at the Combinatorial Matrix Analysis Conference held at the [[University of Victoria]] in British Columbia, Canada, May 20–23, 1987,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Thompson|first=Robert C.|date=1988|title=Editorial|url=https://ilasic.org/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image1.pdf|journal=IMAGE: The Bulletin of the International Matrix Group|volume=1|pages=1}}</ref> hosted by Dale Olesky and [[Pauline van den Driessche]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brualdi|first1=R.|last2=Schneider|first2=H.|date=1988|title=Preface|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0024379588902327/pdfft?md5=8353e32f6c00db78b30a9e16a3fab156&pid=1-s2.0-0024379588902327-main.pdf|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume=107|pages=1|doi=10.1016/0024-3795(88)90232-7|doi-access=free}}</ref>  ILAS was initially known as the International Matrix Group, founded in 1987.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Brualdi|first=Richard|title=Hans Schneider, 1927-2014|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201511/rnoti-p1380.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|year=2015|volume=62|issue=11|pages=1380|doi=10.1090/noti1296|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://legacy.lib.utexas.edu/taro/utcah/03194/cah-03194.html|title=A Guide to the International Linear Algebra Society Records, 1988-2011|website=Briscoe Center for American History|publisher=University of Texas at Austin|access-date=March 21, 2020}}</ref>  The founding officers of ILAS were [[Hans Schneider (mathematician)|Hans Schneider]], President; Robert C. Thompson, Vice President; [[Daniel Hershkowitz]], Secretary;<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Schneider|first=H.|date=1989|title=New Name for International Matrix Group|url=https://ilasic.org/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image2.pdf|journal=IMAGE: The Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society|volume=2|pages=2}}</ref> and James R. Weaver, Treasurer.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Brualdi|first=R.|date=2000|title=Tribute to Jim Weaver|url=https://ilasic.org/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image24.pdf|journal=IMAGE: The Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society|volume=24|pages=3}}</ref>

==ILAS Conferences==

The inaugural meeting of ILAS took place at [[Brigham Young University]] (including one day at the Sundance Mountain Resort) in Provo, Utah, USA, from August 12–15, 1989.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Barrett|first=W.|date=1990|title=ILAS Inaugural Conference Held at BYU|url=https://ilasic.org/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image4.pdf|journal=IMAGE: Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society|volume=4|pages=1}}</ref> The organizing committee consisted of Wayne Barrett, Daniel Hershkowitz, Charles Johnson, Hans Schneider, and Robert C. Thompson.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Barrett|first1=W.|last2=Robinson|first2=D.|last3=Hershkowitz|first3=D.|date=1991|title=Inaugural Conference of the International Linear Algebra Society|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume=150|pages=463–550|doi=10.1016/0024-3795(91)90185-Y|doi-access=free}}</ref>  Much additional support came from Don Robinson, Chair of the BYU Mathematics Department, and James R. Weaver, ILAS Treasurer.<ref name=":0" />  The conference received support from Brigham Young University, the [[National Security Agency]], and the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Barrett|first1=W.|last2=Hershkowitz|first2=D.|last3=Robinson|first3=D.| 
 date=1991|title=Preface|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/002437959190156Q/pdfft?md5=cbbc088bd2d0efe2868b1bdb47b4588e&pid=1-s2.0-002437959190156Q-main.pdf|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume=150|issue=1 |pages=1|doi=10.1016/0024-3795(91)90156-Q|doi-access=free}}</ref> There were 85 in attendance at the conference from 15 countries including [[Olga Taussky-Todd]], a renowned mathematician in Matrix Theory.<ref name=":0" />  The proceedings of the Conference appeared in volume 150 of the journal ''[[Linear Algebra and Its Applications]]''.

The 2nd ILAS conference was held in Lisbon, Portugal,  August 3–7, 1992.  The chair of the organizing committee was José Dias da Silva.  There were 150 participants from 27 countries and the conference was supported by 11 different organizations.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=da Silva|first1=J.D.|last2=Li|first2=C.-K.|last3=de Oliveira|first3=G.|date=1994|title=Preface|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0024379594904782/pdfft?md5=78636ff0115aaa3ebee33edcc0e1c83d&pid=1-s2.0-0024379594904782-main.pdf|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume=197|pages=1}}</ref>  The proceedings of the conference can be found in volumes 197–198 of ''[[Linear Algebra and Its Applications]]''. 

ILAS conferences were held the next 4 years, alternating between the United States and Europe, before beginning the standard pattern of holding the Conference two of every three years (with a few exceptions).  The number of participants at each ILAS conference has grown steadily through the years.

The first ILAS conference outside of the United States and Europe was held in Haifa, Israel in 2001.  The first in the Far East was in Shanghai in 2007 and the first in Latin America was in Cancun, Mexico in 2008. The complete list of locations hosting ILAS conferences follows:<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/conferences/|title=ILAS Conferences|date=25 November 2020 |access-date=April 2, 2021}}</ref> {{div col|colwidth=25em}}

==Prizes and Special Lectures==

ILAS has three prizes named after giants in Linear Algebra.

* '''The Hans Schneider Prize.''' A distinctive feature of the 3rd ILAS meeting held at the [[University of West Florida]] in Pensacola, Florida, March 17–20, 1993, was the institution of the [[Hans Schneider Prize in Linear Algebra|Hans Schneider Prize]]. This prize was initiated thanks to a donation to ILAS from [[Hans Schneider (mathematician)|Hans Schneider]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/hs-guidelines/|title=Guidelines for the Hans Schneider Prize|date=April 2, 2021|website=International Linear Algebra Society}}</ref>  the first president of ILAS and a founding editor of the journal ''[[Linear Algebra and Its Applications]]''. Typically, the prize is awarded every 3 years and has evolved as a prize to recognize a person's career.

* '''The ILAS Olga Taussky and John Todd Prize.''' [[Olga Taussky-Todd]] and [[John (Jack) Todd|John Todd]] have had a decisive impact on the development of theoretical and numerical linear algebra for over half a century. The ILAS Olga Taussky and John Todd Prize honors them for their many and varied mathematical achievements and for their efforts in promoting linear algebra and matrix theory. The prize is awarded once every three to four years recognizing a linear algebra researcher in their mid career. The ILAS Olga Taussky and John Todd Prize was originally referred to as the Taussky–Todd lecture, and was instituted at the 3rd ILAS meeting held at the University of West Florida in Pensacola, Florida, March 17–20, 1993.

* '''The ILAS Richard A. Brualdi Early Career Prize.''' The prize is named for [[Richard A. Brualdi]], who has had a major impact on the field, especially in combinatorial matrix theory. In addition, he has been instrumental to the success of ILAS since its inception. The ILAS Richard A. Brualdi Early Career Prize was instituted in 2021 and is awarded every three years to an outstanding early career researcher in the field of linear algebra, for distinguished contributions to the field.

In addition ILAS awards Special Lectures at ILAS conferences as well as conferences of collaborating mathematics organizations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/special-lectures-support/|title=Special Lectures/Support – International Linear Algebra Society|date=October 19, 2022|website=International Linear Algebra Society}}</ref>

==Publications==

ILAS publishes an electronic journal – the '''''[[Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra]] (ELA'')''',<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://journals.uwyo.edu/index.php/ela/index|title=Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra|website=Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra}}</ref> founded in 1996.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Jackson|first=Allyn|date=2000|title=The Slow Revolution of the Free Electronic Journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/200009/fea-eljnl.pdf|journal=Notices of the AMS|volume=47|pages=1053–1059|via=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> The first Editors-in-Chief were [[Volker Mehrmann]] and [[Daniel Hershkowitz]].<ref name=":2" />  ''ELA'' is a [[Open access|platinum open access]] journal, meaning that it is free to all: no subscription and no article processing fee or page charges. ''ELA'' is an all-electronic journal that welcomes high quality mathematical articles that contribute new insights to matrix analysis and the various aspects of linear algebra and its applications. ''ELA'' sets high standards for refereeing while using conventional refereeing of articles that is carried out electronically.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://journals.uwyo.edu/index.php/ela/about|title=About the Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra|access-date=March 27, 2020}}</ref>

ILAS also produces and distributes '''''IMAGE''','' a semiannual electronic bulletin founded in 1988 with Robert C. Thompson as its first Editor.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Day|first=Jane M.|date=1997|title=Robert C. Thompson, 1931–1995|journal=Linear and Multilinear Algebra|volume=43|issue=1–3|pages=13–18|doi=10.1080/03081089708818513}}</ref> ''IMAGE'' contains: essays related to linear algebra activities; feature articles; interviews of linear algebra experts; book reviews; brief reports on conferences; ILAS business notices; announcements of upcoming workshops and conferences; problems and solutions; and news about individual members.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/image/|title=IMAGE – ILAS' Bulletin|work=International Linear Algebra Society |date=25 November 2020 |access-date=April 2, 2021}}</ref>

==Collaborations with other mathematics organizations==

ILAS collaborates with the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM), the [[American Mathematical Society]] (AMS) and the [[International Workshop on Operator Theory and its Applications]] (IWOTA).

The collaboration with SIAM started in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.siam.org/meetings/la00/|title=Seventh SIAM Conference on Applied Linear Algebra|website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics Archive|access-date=March 21, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brualdi|first1=R.|last2=Hershkowitz|first2=D.|date=1999|title=ILAS President/Vice-President's Annual Report April 1999|url=https://ilasic.org/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image22.pdf|journal=IMAGE: The Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society|volume=22|pages=6–7}}</ref> The SIAM Activity Group on Linear Algebra (SIAG/LA) holds a conference every three years<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://siags.siam.org/siagla/meetings/siamla.html|title=SIAM Activity Group on Linear Algebra|website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|access-date=March 11, 2020}}</ref> (when the year minus 2000 is divisible by 3). As part of the agreement, and to encourage interaction between ILAS and SIAG/LA members, the two societies do not hold conferences in the same year. As a result, ILAS holds conferences two out of every three years. In addition, the two societies exchange speakers with ILAS sponsoring two ILAS speakers at every triennial SIAM Applied Linear Algebra (SIAM ALA) meeting (organized by SIAG/LA) and with SIAM sponsoring a SIAM speaker at every ILAS conference.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Brualdi|first1=R.|last2=Hershkowitz|first2=D.|last3=Horn|first3=R.|date=2001|title=ILAS President/Vice Presidents' Annual Report: April 2001|url=https://ilasic.org/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE/image26.pdf|journal=IMAGE: The Bulletin of the International Linear Algebra Society|volume=26|pages=30–32}}</ref> The first ILAS speakers at a SIAM ALA meeting were [[Hans Schneider (mathematician)|Hans Schneider]] and Hugo Woerdeman in 2000,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/non-ilas-lecturers/|title=The ILAS lecturers at non-ILAS conferences|date=2 January 2021 |access-date=April 2, 2021}}</ref> and the first SIAM speakers at an ILAS conference were [[Michele Benzi]] and [[Misha Kilmer]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Uhlig|first=Frank|date=2004|title=Report on the 10th ILAS Conference 'Challenges in Matrix Theory' at Auburn University in June 2002|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume=379|pages=503–535|doi=10.1016/j.laa.2003.10.002|doi-access=free}}</ref>

The collaboration with AMS started in late 2020 with the establishment of
ILAS as a partner in the [[Joint Mathematics Meetings]] (JMM). In this capacity
ILAS will support a speaker for the "ILAS Lecture" at the JMM to be
selected by ILAS. In addition, at least four special sessions at the JMM will be
identified as ILAS special sessions, the contents of which will be determined by ILAS.
The partnership took effect starting with the JMM 2022 held virtually.

The collaboration with IWOTA started in 2017 with the establishment of the Israel Gohberg ILAS-IWOTA Lecture, which is funded by donations. This lecture series consists of biennial lectures either at an ILAS conference or at an IWOTA meeting. [[Israel Gohberg]] was the founding president of IWOTA and an active member of ILAS.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bart|first1=H.|last2=Dym|first2=H.|last3=Kaaschoek|first3=R.|last4=Lancaster|first4=P.|last5=Markus|first5=A.|last6=Rodman|first6=L.|date=2010|title=In memoriam Israel Gohberg August 23, 1928 – October 12, 2009|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume=433|issue=5|pages=877–892|doi=10.1016/j.laa.2010.03.006|doi-access=free}}</ref> The first Israel Gohberg ILAS-IWOTA Lecturer was [[Vern Paulsen]] at the 2021 IWOTA Lancaster UK meeting.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/ilas-iwota-lecturers/|title=The Israel Gohberg ILAS-IWOTA Lecturers|date=2 January 2021 |access-date=April 2, 2021}}</ref>
